relevance_note: Cohort of 26 IEI patients in which one individual, P22, carries 'TNFAIP3:c.2152del' and has individual-level clinical data (type 1 diabetes, Table 1, Tables S1-S4).
method_note: Read the whole Markdown (main text, Table 1, supplementary Tables S1-S4) by hand; a short Python script only assembled the JSON and checked spans. Cohort of 26 IEI patients; only P22 carries a TNFAIP3 variant, so only P22 gets rows (other 25 patients out of scope, counted in cohort_size_as_stated). No relatives of P22 are described. CONTRADICTION (sex): Table 1 row P22 gives Sex 'M', while Table S3 ('| P22 | 4Y  | F   |') and Table S4 give 'F'; sex left 'not reported'. (Text says '15 males and 11 females'; Table 1 counts 16 M/10 F, S3 counts 15 M/11 F.) Table 1 cell for P22 reads 'TNFAIP3:c.2152del(40m)Hypergly' (stray text, likely conversion/print artefact); variant taken as 'c.2152del' (also in Tables S1/S2). The paper never uses the term HA20/A20 haploinsufficiency for P22; disease label recorded as the stated 'type 1 diabetes'. Age at onset '40' comes from Table 1 column 'Age at onset (month)'; age at diagnosis '40m' from column 'Mutation (Age atdiagnosis)' (text calls it age at genetic diagnosis); age at last evaluation '4Y' is the 'Age' column of Table S3/S4 (immunological testing), assumed to be the study evaluation. Ethnicity 'Chinese' and pathogenicity 'pathogenic' come from cohort-level statements covering all 26 patients. Autoantibodies: routine (ELISA/IFA) autoantibody tests negative for P22 (row 'excluded' for the routine panel), but the antigen microarray showed significantly elevated autoantibodies (row 'observed'); treated as different assays, not a contradiction, and checklist 'autoantibodies (ANA/other)' set observed. Discussion states 'nine patients lacked detectable autoantibodies on routine clinical screening and exhibited no overt autoimmune symptoms' without names, which conflicts with Results naming P22 (type 1 diabetes) among nine microarray-positive patients; not used for any value. Empty Table 1 cells (Infection, Digestive, Lymphoproliferative) treated as not reported; recurrent infections excluded only from the Discussion sentence about the single TNFAIP3 patient. The '#' and '$' marks in Tables S3/S4 are not defined in any legend, so no laboratory abnormalities were extracted. Count-only group statements (e.g. hypothyroidism in two patients, peptic ulcers in P3-P5) were not used to exclude features for P22. Eczema counted as observed for the composite checklist item 'skin lesions'.
